Sheet "Steps": the empty Formula workbook's steps, as it ships.
Sheet "Parameters"
  Excel Table "Parameters", A1:B2
    Headers: name | value
    Row 2:  | 
  D1: Parameters: the fixed values your formulas use, one row per value. Put its name under name and the value under value, such as tax_rate and 0.2 (a plain number, not 20%), then read it by name in a formula: XLOOKUP("tax_rate", Parameters[name], Parameters[value]). Leave the Table empty if no formula uses a fixed value. See step 6 on the Steps sheet.
Sheet "Keys"
  Excel Table "Keys", A1:B2
    Headers: table | key_columns
    Row 2:  | 
  D1: Keys: only for a Table where a value was typed over a formula. Add one row for that Table, however many values were typed over in it: the Table's name under table, and under key_columns the typed column or columns that tell its rows apart, separated by commas, such as job_runs with run_id, or sales with region, month. Copilot uses them to find the row a typed value belongs to. If no column tells the rows apart, leave the Table out. A Table with no value typed over a formula needs no row here. See step 10 on the Steps sheet.
Sheet "job_runs"
  Excel Table "job_runs", A1:F10
    Headers: run_id | job_id | status | duration_mins | avg_retry_secs | dt
    Row 2: 95 | 1 | SUCCESS | 12 | 2 | 2026-09-23 00:00:00
    Row 3: 96 | 2 | SUCCESS | 18 | 0 | 2026-09-23 00:00:00
    Row 4: 97 | 3 | FAILED | 30 | 8 | 2026-09-23 00:00:00
    Row 5: 98 | 2 |  | 15 |  | 2026-09-23 00:00:00
    Row 6: 99 | 1 | TEST | 5 | 0 | 2026-09-23 00:00:00
    Row 7: 101 | 1 | SUCCESS | 10 | 1 | 2026-09-24 00:00:00
    Row 8: 102 | 2 | FAILED | 20 | 6 | 2026-09-24 00:00:00
    Row 9: 103 | 3 | SUCCESS | 30 | 0 | 2026-09-24 00:00:00
    Row 10: 104 | 1 | SUCCESS | 40 | 3 | 2026-09-24 00:00:00
Sheet "Pivot"
  PivotTable "PivotTable1", A3:G7
    Source: Excel Table "job_runs"
    Rows: Years, dt
    Columns: duration_mins
    Value "Sum of duration_mins": Sum of duration_mins
    Field "duration_mins" groups duration_mins By 10, Starting at 0, Ending at 49
    Field "dt" groups dt By Months, Starting at 2026-09-23 00:00:00, Ending at 2026-09-25 00:00:00
    Field "Years" groups dt By Years, Starting at 2026-09-23 00:00:00, Ending at 2026-09-25 00:00:00
    Totals shown: Grand Total row, Grand Total column, subtotals of Years
    Cells: each value cell, what Excel last stored in it, then the Value it shows and the Rows and Columns items it stands for:
      B5: 5 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026; Columns duration_mins 0-9)
      C5: 55 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026; Columns duration_mins 10-19)
      D5: 20 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026; Columns duration_mins 20-29)
      E5: 60 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026; Columns duration_mins 30-39)
      F5: 40 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026; Columns duration_mins 40-49)
      G5: 180 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026; Columns Grand Total)
      B6: 5 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026, dt Sep; Columns duration_mins 0-9)
      C6: 55 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026, dt Sep; Columns duration_mins 10-19)
      D6: 20 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026, dt Sep; Columns duration_mins 20-29)
      E6: 60 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026, dt Sep; Columns duration_mins 30-39)
      F6: 40 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026, dt Sep; Columns duration_mins 40-49)
      G6: 180 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Years 2026, dt Sep; Columns Grand Total)
      B7: 5 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Grand Total; Columns duration_mins 0-9)
      C7: 55 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Grand Total; Columns duration_mins 10-19)
      D7: 20 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Grand Total; Columns duration_mins 20-29)
      E7: 60 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Grand Total; Columns duration_mins 30-39)
      F7: 40 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Grand Total; Columns duration_mins 40-49)
      G7: 180 (Sum of duration_mins; Rows Grand Total; Columns Grand Total)
Order, each piece after every piece it reads:
  1. Excel Table "Parameters"
  2. Excel Table "Keys"
  3. Excel Table "job_runs"
  4. PivotTable "PivotTable1", reads Excel Table "job_runs"
Each final's query reads the steps it needs as CTEs in this order, each CTE after every CTE it reads.
